plugin.pbkdf2.title: PBKDF2
plugin.pbkdf2.preset.rfc6070-tc5: RFC 6070 test 5: long password and salt, 25 bytes (two blocks)
plugin.pbkdf2.param.macHint: The pseudorandom function: HMAC over one of the hash functions.
plugin.pbkdf2.param.passwordEncodingHint: Text is encoded as UTF-8; hex gives the bytes directly.
plugin.pbkdf2.param.passwordHint: At most 128 bytes. A teaching tool: never type a real password here.
plugin.pbkdf2.param.saltEncodingHint: Text is encoded as UTF-8; hex gives the bytes directly.
plugin.pbkdf2.param.saltHint: At most 128 bytes; public, but different for every password.
plugin.pbkdf2.param.iterationsHint: 1 to 100000. Every iteration is one more HMAC call per block.
plugin.pbkdf2.op.u1: U1 – HMAC of the salt and the block number
plugin.pbkdf2.op.u: U – HMAC of the previous U
plugin.pbkdf2.step.initial_one: PBKDF2 with {{mac}} as the PRF stretches a password of {{passwordBytes}} bytes and a salt of {{saltBytes}} bytes into a key of {{length}} bytes: one block T, the XOR of c = {{iterations}} HMAC outputs. This lab is a teaching tool, not a place for real passwords: never type one here.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.initial_other: PBKDF2 with {{mac}} as the PRF stretches a password of {{passwordBytes}} bytes and a salt of {{saltBytes}} bytes into a key of {{length}} bytes: {{count}} blocks T, each the XOR of c = {{iterations}} HMAC outputs. This lab is a teaching tool, not a place for real passwords: never type one here.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.u1: Block {{block}}, iteration 1: U1 = {{mac}}(P, S ‖ INT({{block}})), the salt followed by the block number as four big-endian bytes ({{counter}}). The password is the HMAC key; its two midstates were computed once and are reused by every call. F starts as U1.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.u: Iteration {{j}} of {{iterations}}: U{{j}} = HMAC(P, U{{previous}}). The keyed midstates are cloned, not recomputed, so this call costs two compressions.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.xor: F = F ⊕ U{{j}}: F now holds U1 ⊕ … ⊕ U{{j}}.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.skip: U{{first}} … U{{last}}: {{hidden}} HMAC calls, not shown. U and F show the real values after iteration {{last}}.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.block: T{{block}} = F: its {{bytes}} bytes go into DK at offset {{offset}}.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.blockTruncated: T{{block}} = F, but DK needs only {{bytes}} more bytes: the first {{bytes}} of its {{size}} bytes go into DK at offset {{offset}}.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.output_one: DK = T1, {{length}} bytes. That took {{calls}} {{mac}} calls (one block × c = {{iterations}}) and, after the two midstates, exactly {{compressions}} compressions: 2 for each of U2 … Uc, and for U1 as many as S ‖ INT(i) and the digest need blocks (with padding). An attacker who guesses passwords pays the same for every guess.
plugin.pbkdf2.step.output_other: DK = T1 ‖ … ‖ T{{count}}, {{length}} bytes. That took {{calls}} {{mac}} calls ({{count}} blocks × c = {{iterations}}) and, after the two midstates, exactly {{compressions}} compressions: 2 for each of U2 … Uc, and for U1 as many as S ‖ INT(i) and the digest need blocks (with padding). An attacker pays only c = {{iterations}} calls per guess: one block is enough to test a guess.

plugin.pbkdf2.error.invalidParams: Give the PRF, password, salt, iteration count and key length as text.
plugin.pbkdf2.error.mac: Choose an HMAC function as the PRF.
plugin.pbkdf2.error.encoding: Choose text or hex for the password and the salt.
plugin.pbkdf2.error.passwordLength: The password has {{length}} bytes; at most {{max}} are allowed.
plugin.pbkdf2.error.saltLength: The salt has {{length}} bytes; at most {{max}} are allowed.
plugin.pbkdf2.error.iterations: The iteration count must be a whole number from {{min}} to {{max}}.
plugin.pbkdf2.error.length: The key length must be a whole number of bytes from {{min}} to {{max}}.
plugin.pbkdf2.error.notHmac: {{id}} is not an HMAC function; PBKDF2 here uses HMAC as its PRF.
